title: FestivalIndex
description: Schema for the repo-root index.json, a generated summary of every festival.json in the repo. Meant for multi-festival selection UIs: enough header info to list/sort/filter festivals plus cheap aggregate counts, without loading every full festival.json. This file is generated by scripts/generate-index.py — do not hand-edit it.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this index schema (not of any individual festival). Bump when the shape of an entry changes.

generatedAt.description: UTC timestamp of the generation run that produced this file.

festivals.description: One entry per festival.json found in the repo, sorted by earliest festivalDays entry (soonest first), then by name.

id.description: The festival.json's own globally unique id, e.g. 'summer-breeze-2026'.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the source festival.json, e.g. 'summer-breeze/2026/festival.json'.

version.description: The source festival.json's own 'version' field, so consumers can detect the source data changed independently of this index.

visible.description: The source festival.json's own 'visible' field (defaults to true when absent there). Carried through rather than filtered out so a consumer can choose to show hidden/test festivals behind a developer or tester mode; normal-mode UIs should filter these out client-side.

festivalDays.description: Full copy of the festival's ISO festivalDays, in order. First/last entries give the date range; the full list lets a consumer avoid re-deriving day-by-day scheduling info just to show 'runs Mon-Fri'.

isMultiStage.description: True if the source data has more than one stage (stages.length > 1).

translationLangs.description: BCP 47 language tags with a translations[] entry in the source data, e.g. ['de']. Empty array if none.

counts.description: Cheap aggregate counts, so a picker can show e.g. '135 artists' without loading the full festival.json.

links.description: Total links[] entries, global and per-artist combined.

globalLinks.description: Subset of links[] with no artistId (shown on the Home screen).

topGenres.description: Up to 10 most common artist genre tags, mapping genre name to number of artists with that genre. Ordered by count descending, then genre name ascending. Empty object if the festival has no artists with genres.

completeness.description: Derived 'how much is there to see yet' signal for pickers, so users know what to expect before opening a freshly-added festival. Computed purely from existing festival.json fields -- no manual input. Content (lineup, pictures, descriptions, links) and schedule (running order, per-artist times) are scored on independent axes and combined, because in practice content fills in well before the schedule does; see AGENTS.md 'Completeness / stars'.

stars.description: 1 (freshly announced stub) to 5 (lineup, pictures, descriptions, links and full running order all present). Derived from contentLevel x scheduleLevel -- see AGENTS.md for the combination table.

contentLevel.description: 'none' = no artists announced yet. 'complete' = artistInfoCoverage >= 0.9. 'partial' = anything in between.

scheduleLevel.description: 'none' = runningOrderExists is false. 'full' = runningOrderExists is true and scheduleCoverage >= 0.9. 'partial' = runningOrderExists is true but coverage hasn't caught up yet (schedule being rolled out gradually).

artistInfoCoverage.description: Fraction of artists[] with both imageUrl and description non-empty. 0 if there are no artists yet.

scheduleCoverage.description: Fraction of artists[] with startTime set. 0 if there are no artists yet.

lineup.description: Derived popularity profile of the lineup, computed from the artist registry's 1-10 'popularity' scores (matched via artists[].globalId). Omitted when no artist of the festival has a score yet. 'top' and 'depth' are stable enum keys the client maps to localized display text and combines (e.g. strong + discovery -> 'discovery-heavy, with big names on top'); see AGENTS.md 'Lineup profile'.

depth.description: What is behind the top, first match wins: 'underground' = discovery >= 0.8; 'deep' = core >= 0.6; 'solid' = core >= 0.45; 'discovery' = discovery >= 0.4; otherwise 'mixed'.

headliners.description: Mean popularity of the (up to) 3 most popular scored artists, rounded to 1 decimal.

core.description: Share of scored artists with popularity >= 5 (proven acts).

discovery.description: Share of scored artists with popularity <= 3 (lesser-known acts).

scoredArtists.description: Number of artists[] that resolved to a registry entry with a popularity score; the denominator of core and discovery.

lowConfidence.description: True when scoredArtists < 10 -- with so few acts a single band moves the shares a lot, so clients may want to soften the label.
